Most revenue comes from financial product transaction revenue of ¥331,041 million, which combines interest on loans, card customer fees and credit guarantee fees; other revenue includes service transaction revenue of ¥6,668 million, such as ATM fees and Mastercard merchant fees. Interest on loans is recognized on an accrual basis, while card customer fees and credit guarantee fees are recognized on an outstanding-balance basis, calculated by applying a prescribed rate to the principal balance. entries.709a7fcd384a5ab8: The company, together with six [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] and one equity-method affiliate, forms a group that provides financial services across four [[term:segment|reportable segments]]. Its main business is unsecured personal loans and MasterCard® credit cards, supplemented by loan guarantees for loans from partner banks and others, overseas financing in Asia, and the management and collection of receivables. Of operating revenue of ¥337,709 million for the fiscal year ended March 2026, financial product transaction revenue, which combines interest on loans, card fees and credit guarantee fees, accounted for ¥331,041 million. Because the company lends money it has borrowed, the procurement of funds and the management of losses from loans that are not repaid (bad-debt expenses) form the foundation of its business. The company is a consolidated subsidiary of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, and it is positioned as a core company in the group's consumer finance business.

The company, together with six consolidated subsidiaries and one equity-method affiliate, forms a group. As of March 31, 2026, consolidated employees numbered 5,626 (in addition, the average annual number of fixed-term contract employees was 122). Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, Inc. (hereinafter 'MUFG') is the parent company, holding 40.18% of voting rights (of which 2.60% is held indirectly), and there is a capital and business alliance under a basic agreement dated September 2008. Under this agreement, when the company takes actions that change the number of voting rights, such as issuing new shares, it must consult MUFG in advance, and matters such as business transfers, mergers, capital alliances and business alliances require MUFG's prior approval. There is also a memorandum requiring MUFG's prior approval for matters resolved at shareholders' meetings. On the other hand, the securities report states that management policies and business strategies are decided by the company on its own judgment, based on the parent's management policies, and that the company secures its independence as a listed company.
